You are the cold-reviewer role screening a draft process definition against its fitness set, round 2, in a fresh context. You know nothing of prior rounds and must not seek anything about them. Working directory: /home/vscode/rebaseline.

Read the criteria set and the artifact — and NOTHING else (no other files, no searches):
- criteria_path: basis/fitness/process-definition.fitness.md
- artifact: basis/processes/skill-rendering.md

State, as judge_stamp, the model and prompt version you judge as. Judge the artifact against every scenario of the criteria set. Report every finding with the criterion it fails by name, the quoted text, the change you propose, and whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the deciding role decides from the review. A defect no criterion names is a finding with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean" only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top three changes.

Return your review as YAML matching the screen-review type exactly:

```yaml
judge_stamp: "<model id> / process-definition screen"
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
  - criterion: "<scenario name or 'uncovered'>"
    quote: "<quoted text; whole passage if wobbly>"
    change: "<the repair you propose>"
    decidability: confident | wobbly
top_changes: ["<up to three>"]
```

Do not edit any file. Your final message is the YAML and nothing else.

- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. - run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Fitness set: process-definition

These scenarios are evaluated by the `cold-reviewer` role, never
executed; the compiler and linter carry the mechanical half of the
same requirements. The mapping table compiles each Then into the
judge-rubric assertion the reviewer scores. The scenarios project the
[process-definition typedef](../artifacts/process-definition.md)'s
requirements and the
[process-definition guideline](../guidelines/process-definition.md)'s
rules into a judge's rubric.

## Scenarios

Scenario 1: the definition is the single source its renderings claim
  Given the process definition, its flow diagram, and its rendered
  skill
  When the diagram and skill are compared to the steps section
  Then both correspond to the steps exactly — every step, prompt, and
  branch present, nothing added — and both declare themselves
  generated, never hand-edited

Scenario 2: every outcome has a live witness
  Given the outcomes list and the steps section
  When each outcome's named witness is looked up
  Then every outcome names a step, check, or branch that exists, and a
  reader can say from the witness alone whether the outcome held for a
  run

Scenario 3: every loop declares its exits
  Given every cycle in the flow
  When its branch rows are read
  Then each cycle carries a labeled reached-state success exit, a
  round or budget cap, or both — no loop can run unbounded

Scenario 4: steps read only what they list
  Given each step's prompt, checks, and run template
  When every reference in them is resolved
  Then each resolves to a declared input or output of that step, and
  no prompt directs the agent to load undeclared context

Scenario 5: the run returns the artifact
  Given the result declaration and the purpose
  When they are compared
  Then the run returns the artifact it exists to produce, or result is
  absent and the outcomes pin the run's value

Scenario 6: prose sits where prose belongs
  Given every step record and the guiding statement
  When each is read
  Then step prose appears only in prompt fields, and the guiding
  statement (when present) states a cross-step judgment, never a
  sequence

## Compile mapping (each Then/And → one judge-rubric assertion)

| Scenario Then | Judge-rubric assertion |
|---|---|
| 1 — renderings correspond | "Walk the diagram and skill against the steps: name any step, prompt, or branch missing or added, and any rendering not marked generated. Empty list = pass." |
| 2 — outcomes witnessed | "For each outcome, name the witnessing step/check/branch and confirm it exists. Any outcome with a missing or unverifiable witness = fail, cite it." |
| 3 — loop exits declared | "List every cycle and its labeled exits. Any cycle without a success exit or cap = fail, cite it." |
| 4 — declared reads only | "For each step, quote any reference in prompt/checks/run that is not a declared input or output, and any prompt directing undeclared context loads. Empty list = pass." |
| 5 — artifact result | "Name the result value and what the purpose says the run produces. Mismatch, or a status-shaped result = fail; absent result justified by value-pinning outcomes = pass." |
| 6 — prose placement | "Quote any prose in a step outside prompt, and quote the guiding statement if it sequences steps. Empty list = pass." |

## Sources

Gherkin syntax (readable G/W/T frame — syntax only, no runner);
G-Eval–style rubric decomposition for the mapping table; the tests
project the process-definition typedef's checklist and Commitment and
the guideline's rules, per the definition-chain shape the
principle-set chain established.

Every approved process definition has its loadable skill at the 38 load point, byte-equal to a fresh render of that definition — 39 witnessed by `route`'s success exit on empty `findings`. 40 - O2. An agent beginning an activity loads that activity's skill: 41 availability is placement at the load point, and a skill absent from 42 it is a `missing` finding, never assumed loadable — witnessed by 43 `check`'s run and `reconcile`'s renders into `load_point`. 44 - O3. A definition that does not stand approved yields no loadable 45 skill: `enumerate` admits only approved definitions, and a skill 46 whose source is not among them is a `stale` finding removed at 47 reconciliation — witnessed by `enumerate`'s run and the stale rows 48 of `findings` consumed by `reconcile`. 49 - O4. Every finding names its process or the rendering home it stands 50 in, and reaches its consumer — the 51 reconciliation (re-render or removal) or, for a definition that will 52 not compile or names no skill id, the owner, as a review entry in 53 that definition's Document History — witnessed by `check`'s output 54 and the `reconcile` and `report` prompts with `escalations`. 55 - O5. The load point is the one rendering home: a second home standing 56 is a finding, its removal is a reconciliation act, and the index 57 amendment it demands is filed to the owner, never made here — 58 witnessed by the `second-home` row of `findings` and 59 `reconcile`'s prompt. 60 61 **Roles:** reconciler and reporter — 62 [`../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md`](../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md) 63 (the compilers and the lint are this role's apparatus; it consumes the 64 check's findings, and its resulting action per finding is a re-render, 65 a removal, or an escalation). The owner — the product authority — 66 decides every escalated definition change; that decision lands through 67 governed evolution, not through a step of this process. The check 68 itself is mechanical and runs by the runtime against the approved 69 definitions and the compiler's rendering contract, so the definition 70 of good sits outside the role that reconciles. 71 72 **Carried by:** `.claude/skills/skill-rendering/SKILL.md` — generated 73 from this definition by 74 [`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never 75 edited by hand. Self-referential by design: this process renders its 76 own carrier like every other approved definition, and its first run 77 creates it. Until that first run the carrier does not exist, so its 78 correspondence to this definition cannot be walked at screening time: 79 the bootstrap is accepted for the draft, and the process's own first 80 run — its check against a fresh render — is the check of that 81 correspondence. 82 83 ## Flow (compiled) 84 85 Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not 86 edit by hand. 87 88 ```mermaid 89 flowchart TD 90 enumerate["Enumerate the approved definitions — runtime
in — definitions: string
out — approved: string[]"] 91 check["Check the load point against a fresh render — runtime

out — escalations: string[]"]) 96 __end(("end")) 97 __start(("start")) --> enumerate 98 enumerate --> check 99 check --> route 100 route -->|success exit: check clean — every approved process available| __end 101 route -->|failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with findings open| report 102 route -->|else| reconcile 103 reconcile --> advance_round 104 advance_round --> check 105 report --> __end 106 ``` 107 108 109 ## Data 110 111 Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema 112 names inline; conditions are CEL expressions over these names. Paths 113 are relative to the lead shop's repository root, the run's working 114 directory. The *loadable form* of a process definition is the skill 115 the compiler generates from it under the process-definition typedef's 116 rendering contract — front-matter carrying `generated: true`, its 117 source and `source-digest`, and a body of the purpose, guiding 118 statement, diagram, and every step with its prompt verbatim; the term's 119 glossary entry is a filed gap (lead-36apr). `definitions` names the 120 directory of the lead shop's process definitions and nothing else; 121 `load_point` is the one rendering home — the directory the harness 122 loads skills from, so placement there is availability. `retired_home` 123 is the second rendering home this process retires so that no second 124 copy can diverge: while the directory exists its presence is a 125 finding, its removal belongs to `reconcile`, and the amendments the 126 removal demands — the basis index's `skills/` entry and every Carried 127 by reference still pointing there — are resulting actions filed to 128 the owner, never edits this process makes. The compiler regenerates a 129 definition's in-document flow diagram on every invocation; for a 130 definition whose diagram is current that write is byte-identical. An 131 approved definition that names no `carried-by` skill id cannot render 132 — at authoring time seven approved definitions stand so — and each is 133 a first-run finding escalated to the owner. The run declares no 134 `result`: `produces` is empty because the run's value is state change 135 — every approved definition available at the load point — and O1's 136 witness pins it. 137 138 ```yaml 139 data: 140 definitions: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/processes} 141 compiler: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/tools/compile_process.py} 142 load_point: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: .claude/skills} 143 retired_home: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/skills} 144 approved: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 145 findings: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 146 escalations: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 147 round: {type: integer, initial: 1} 148 round_cap: {type: integer, initial: 3} 149 ``` 150 151 ## Steps 152 153 ```yaml 154 start: enumerate 155 steps: 156 - id: enumerate 157 name: Enumerate the approved definitions 158 run-by: {execution: runtime} 159 inputs: [definitions] 160 outputs: [approved] 161 run: | 162 grep -l '^status: approved' ${definitions}/*.md | sort 163 next: check 164 165 - id: check 166 name: Check the load point against a fresh render 167 run-by: {execution: runtime} 168 inputs: [approved, load_point, retired_home, compiler] 169 outputs: [findings] 170 run: | 171 scratch=$(mktemp -d) 172 for def in ${approved}; do 173 pid=$(sed -n 's/^id: //p' "$def" | head -1) 174 name=$(sed -n 's/^carried-by: //p' "$def" | sed 's/-skill$//') 175 if [ -z "$name" ]; then echo "missing $pid no-skill-id"; continue; fi 176 if ! python3 ${compiler} "$def" --skill "$scratch/$name/SKILL.md" >/dev/null 2>&1; then 177 echo "will-not-compile $pid"; continue 178 fi 179 if [ ! -f "${load_point}/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then echo "missing $pid"; continue; fi 180 diff -q "$scratch/$name/SKILL.md" "${load_point}/$name/SKILL.md" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "diverged $pid" 181 done 182 for f in "${load_point}"/*/SKILL.md; do 183 [ -f "$f" ] || continue 184 src=$(sed -n 's/^source: //p' "$f") 185 printf '%s\n' ${approved} | grep -qxF -- "$src" || echo "stale $src $f" 186 done 187 if [ -d "${retired_home}" ]; then echo "second-home ${retired_home}"; fi 188 rm -rf "$scratch" 189 next: route 190 191 - id: route 192 name: Route on the findings 193 run-by: {execution: runtime} 194 inputs: [findings, round, round_cap] 195 branches: 196 - label: "success exit: check clean — every approved process available" 197 when: size(findings) == 0 198 next: end 199 - label: "failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with findings open" 200 when: round >= round_cap 201 next: report 202 - else: reconcile 203 204 - id: reconcile 205 name: Reconcile the findings 206 run-by: {role: lead-solutions-architect, execution: agent} 207 inputs: [findings, approved, load_point, retired_home, compiler, escalations] 208 outputs: [escalations] 209 prompt: | 210 Act on each row of findings by kind, skipping any definition 211 already named in escalations. "diverged", or "missing" with a 212 skill id: re-render — run 213 `python3 ${compiler} --skill 214 //SKILL.md`, the definition's path from 215 approved and its carried-by id without the -skill suffix; 216 the render overwrites whatever stands, a hand-edit included — 217 reconciliation is the re-render, never an edit to the skill. 218 "stale": remove that skill's directory from the load point — its 219 source does not stand approved, so nothing of it stays loadable. 220 "second-home": remove the retired home directory, then add to 221 escalations the definition changes the removal demands of the 222 owner — the basis index's skills/ entry and every Carried by 223 reference still pointing there. "will-not-compile", or "missing" 224 marked no-skill-id: do not retry; write a review entry into that 225 definition's Document History naming this process and the 226 defect, and add the definition's path with the entry to 227 escalations. Return escalations. 228 next: advance-round 229 230 - id: advance-round 231 name: Advance the round 232 run-by: {execution: runtime} 233 inputs: [round] 234 set: 235 round: round + 1 236 next: check 237 238 - id: report 239 name: Report the findings left open 240 run-by: {role: lead-solutions-architect, execution: agent} 241 inputs: [findings, approved, escalations] 242 outputs: [escalations] 243 prompt: | 244 Every finding still open at the round cap leaves this run as the 245 owner's. For each row of findings whose definition is not yet 246 named in escalations, write a review entry into that 247 definition's Document History — the definition's path from 248 approved — naming this process and the finding, and add the 249 path with the entry to escalations. The consumer of this report 250 is the solutions architect role, whose re-render has run its 251 course inside this loop; the resulting action on each escalated 252 row is the owner's decision on the named definition. Return 253 escalations. 254 next: end 255 ``` 256 257 ## Derived checks 258 259 | Outcome | Check | Kind | Where | 260 |---|---|---|---| 261 | O1 | the success exit fires exactly on `size(findings) == 0` | mechanical | `route` branches | 262 | O2 | every approved definition without its skill at the load point yields a `missing` row; renders land only under `load_point` | mechanical | `check.run`, `reconcile.prompt` | 263 | O3 | `enumerate` admits only `status: approved`; the stale scan covers every skill at the load point and `reconcile` removes each `stale` row | mechanical | `enumerate.run`, `check.run`, `reconcile.prompt` | 264 | O4 | each finding row names its process or the rendering home it stands in; a will-not-compile or no-skill-id row lands as a review entry in the named definition's Document History and in `escalations` | judged | `check.run`, `reconcile` and `report` prompts | 265 | O5 | a `second-home` row stands while `retired_home` exists; its removal and the filed index amendment are directed in `reconcile.prompt` | judged | `check.run`, `reconcile.prompt` | 266 267 ## Document History 268 269 | Version | Date | Kind | Entry | 270 |---|---|---|---| 271 | 1 | 2026-09-02 | update | Authored under init-skills-availability's assigned feature feat-skills-availability as the initiative's deliverable, per the authority's scope ruling: "This should itself be a process." --- type: process-definition id: skill-rendering-process owner: product-authority status: draft version: 1 created: 2026-09-02 updated: 2026-09-02 produces: [] carried-by: skill-rendering-skill condition-language: cel annotations: claude-code: activation: model-judged promotion: experiment-local use-when: "an approved process definition changes or lands, a loadable skill at the agent's load point stands in doubt — missing, hand-edited, or left by a definition no longer approved — or the shop must confirm that every approved process is available" --- # Process: Skill rendering **Purpose:** Make every approved process definition of the lead shop available at the agent's load point — the `.claude/skills/` directory the harness loads skills from — by checking what stands there against a fresh render of each approved definition and reconciling every difference through the compiler, so that an agent beginning an activity operates from the approved definition of that activity: placement at the load point is what makes the skill load, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that every approved process is available. **Guiding statement:** A rendering is never the source of truth. Whatever stands at the load point that a fresh render of an approved definition would not put there is a finding, and every finding resolves toward the definition — a re-render, a removal, or the owner's decision on the definition — never an edit to a skill. **Outcomes:** - O1. Every approved process definition has its loadable skill at the load point, byte-equal to a fresh render of that definition — witnessed by `route`'s success exit on empty `findings`. - O2. An agent beginning an activity loads that activity's skill: availability is placement at the load point, and a skill absent from it is a `missing` finding, never assumed loadable — witnessed by `check`'s run and `reconcile`'s renders into `load_point`. - O3. A definition that does not stand approved yields no loadable skill: `enumerate` admits only approved definitions, and a skill whose source is not among them is a `stale` finding removed at reconciliation — witnessed by `enumerate`'s run and the stale rows of `findings` consumed by `reconcile`. - O4. Every finding names its process or the rendering home it stands in, and reaches its consumer — the reconciliation (re-render or removal) or, for a definition that will not compile or names no skill id, the owner, as a review entry in that definition's Document History — witnessed by `check`'s output and the `reconcile` and `report` prompts with `escalations`. - O5. The load point is the one rendering home: a second home standing is a finding, its removal is a reconciliation act, and the index amendment it demands is filed to the owner, never made here — witnessed by the `second-home` row of `findings` and `reconcile`'s prompt. **Roles:** reconciler and reporter — [`../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md`](../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md) (the compilers and the lint are this role's apparatus; it consumes the check's findings, and its resulting action per finding is a re-render, a removal, or an escalation). The owner — the product authority — decides every escalated definition change; that decision lands through governed evolution, not through a step of this process. The check itself is mechanical and runs by the runtime against the approved definitions and the compiler's rendering contract, so the definition of good sits outside the role that reconciles. **Carried by:** `.claude/skills/skill-rendering/SKILL.md` — generated from this definition by [`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never edited by hand. Self-referential by design: this process renders its own carrier like every other approved definition, and its first run creates it. Until that first run the carrier does not exist, so its correspondence to this definition cannot be walked at screening time: the bootstrap is accepted for the draft, and the process's own first run — its check against a fresh render — is the check of that correspondence. ## Flow (compiled) Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not edit by hand. ```mermaid flowchart TD enumerate["Enumerate the approved definitions — runtime
in — definitions: string
out — approved: string[]"] check["Check the load point against a fresh render — runtime
in — approved: string[], load_point: string, retired_home: string, compiler: string
out — findings: string[]"] route{"Route on the findings
in — findings: string[], round: integer, round_cap: integer"} reconcile(["Reconcile the findings — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — findings: string[], approved: string[], load_point: string, retired_home: string, compiler: string, escalations: string[]
out — escalations: string[]"]) advance_round["Advance the round — runtime
in — round: integer
sets — round: integer"] report(["Report the findings left open — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — findings: string[], approved: string[], escalations: string[]
out — escalations: string[]"]) __end(("end")) __start(("start")) --> enumerate enumerate --> check check --> route route -->|success exit: check clean — every approved process available| __end route -->|failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with findings open| report route -->|else| reconcile reconcile --> advance_round advance_round --> check report --> __end ``` ## Data Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema names inline; conditions are CEL expressions over these names. Paths are relative to the lead shop's repository root, the run's working directory. The *loadable form* of a process definition is the skill the compiler generates from it under the process-definition typedef's rendering contract — front-matter carrying `generated: true`, its source and `source-digest`, and a body of the purpose, guiding statement, diagram, and every step with its prompt verbatim; the term's glossary entry is a filed gap (lead-36apr). `definitions` names the directory of the lead shop's process definitions and nothing else; `load_point` is the one rendering home — the directory the harness loads skills from, so placement there is availability. `retired_home` is the second rendering home this process retires so that no second copy can diverge: while the directory exists its presence is a finding, its removal belongs to `reconcile`, and the amendments the removal demands — the basis index's `skills/` entry and every Carried by reference still pointing there — are resulting actions filed to the owner, never edits this process makes. The compiler regenerates a definition's in-document flow diagram on every invocation; for a definition whose diagram is current that write is byte-identical. An approved definition that names no `carried-by` skill id cannot render — at authoring time seven approved definitions stand so — and each is a first-run finding escalated to the owner. The run declares no `result`: `produces` is empty because the run's value is state change — every approved definition available at the load point — and O1's witness pins it. ```yaml data: definitions: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/processes} compiler: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/tools/compile_process.py} load_point: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: .claude/skills} retired_home: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/skills} approved: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} findings: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} escalations: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} round: {type: integer, initial: 1} round_cap: {type: integer, initial: 3} ``` ## Steps ```yaml start: enumerate steps: - id: enumerate name: Enumerate the approved definitions run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [definitions] outputs: [approved] run: | grep -l '^status: approved' ${definitions}/*.md | sort next: check - id: check name: Check the load point against a fresh render run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [approved, load_point, retired_home, compiler] outputs: [findings] run: | scratch=$(mktemp -d) for def in ${approved}; do pid=$(sed -n 's/^id: //p' "$def" | head -1) name=$(sed -n 's/^carried-by: //p' "$def" | sed 's/-skill$//') if [ -z "$name" ]; then echo "missing $pid no-skill-id"; continue; fi if ! python3 ${compiler} "$def" --skill "$scratch/$name/SKILL.md" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "will-not-compile $pid"; continue fi if [ ! -f "${load_point}/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then echo "missing $pid"; continue; fi diff -q "$scratch/$name/SKILL.md" "${load_point}/$name/SKILL.md" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "diverged $pid" done for f in "${load_point}"/*/SKILL.md; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue src=$(sed -n 's/^source: //p' "$f") printf '%s\n' ${approved} | grep -qxF -- "$src" || echo "stale $src $f" done if [ -d "${retired_home}" ]; then echo "second-home ${retired_home}"; fi rm -rf "$scratch" next: route - id: route name: Route on the findings run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [findings, round, round_cap] branches: - label: "success exit: check clean — every approved process available" when: size(findings) == 0 next: end - label: "failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with findings open" when: round >= round_cap next: report - else: reconcile - id: reconcile name: Reconcile the findings run-by: {role: lead-solutions-architect, execution: agent} inputs: [findings, approved, load_point, retired_home, compiler, escalations] outputs: [escalations] prompt: | Act on each row of findings by kind, skipping any definition already named in escalations. "diverged", or "missing" with a skill id: re-render — run `python3 ${compiler} --skill //SKILL.md`, the definition's path from approved and its carried-by id without the -skill suffix; the render overwrites whatever stands, a hand-edit included — reconciliation is the re-render, never an edit to the skill. "stale": remove that skill's directory from the load point — its source does not stand approved, so nothing of it stays loadable. "second-home": remove the retired home directory, then add to escalations the definition changes the removal demands of the owner — the basis index's skills/ entry and every Carried by reference still pointing there. "will-not-compile", or "missing" marked no-skill-id: do not retry; write a review entry into that definition's Document History naming this process and the defect, and add the definition's path with the entry to escalations. Return escalations. next: advance-round - id: advance-round name: Advance the round run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [round] set: round: round + 1 next: check - id: report name: Report the findings left open run-by: {role: lead-solutions-architect, execution: agent} inputs: [findings, approved, escalations] outputs: [escalations] prompt: | Every finding still open at the round cap leaves this run as the owner's. For each row of findings whose definition is not yet named in escalations, write a review entry into that definition's Document History — the definition's path from approved — naming this process and the finding, and add the path with the entry to escalations. The consumer of this report is the solutions architect role, whose re-render has run its course inside this loop; the resulting action on each escalated row is the owner's decision on the named definition. Return escalations. next: end ``` ## Derived checks | Outcome | Check | Kind | Where | |---|---|---|---| | O1 | the success exit fires exactly on `size(findings) == 0` | mechanical | `route` branches | | O2 | every approved definition without its skill at the load point yields a `missing` row; renders land only under `load_point` | mechanical | `check.run`, `reconcile.prompt` | | O3 | `enumerate` admits only `status: approved`; the stale scan covers every skill at the load point and `reconcile` removes each `stale` row | mechanical | `enumerate.run`, `check.run`, `reconcile.prompt` | | O4 | each finding row names its process or the rendering home it stands in; a will-not-compile or no-skill-id row lands as a review entry in the named definition's Document History and in `escalations` | judged | `check.run`, `reconcile` and `report` prompts | | O5 | a `second-home` row stands while `retired_home` exists; its removal and the filed index amendment are directed in `reconcile.prompt` | judged | `check.run`, `reconcile.prompt` | ## Document History | Version | Date | Kind | Entry | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 2026-09-02 | update | Authored under init-skills-availability's assigned feature feat-skills-availability as the initiative's deliverable, per the authority's scope ruling: "This should itself be a process." One rendering home decided — the agent's load point, `.claude/skills/` — with `basis/skills/` retired by the run and the index amendment filed to the owner as a resulting action; the seven approved definitions naming no skill id are first-run findings for the owner; "loadable form" defined in Data pending its glossary entry (lead-36apr). |
